topic: How Noah works: a native macOS agent that finds the real cause of a Mac problem and fixes it only after you approve

through_line.name: The issue-card stack
through_line.progression: A pile of identical grey cards, each stamped with a vague phrase, grows beside the laptop as the fake problem count climbs, peaks at the approval moment, then unwinds.
through_line.resolution: In the payoff the stack collapses flat and leaves exactly one card face up, with the actual cause named on it in plain type.

blocks.vo_line: Your Mac is slow. It is probably not junk, and the cleaner you just ran already emptied every cache you have.
blocks.through_line_state: one grey card lying alone beside the trackpad
shots: WIDE eye-level: a sunlit home desk seen across the room, a calm adult seated still at an open laptop, morning light on the wall behind
ECU high: the spinning wait cursor turning on the laptop screen, its colours smeared by the angle
MEDIUM low: the adult leaning back from the desk, one hand lifted off the trackpad, shoulders dropping
CU overhead: a single grey issue card face up on the wood, one vague phrase stamped across it
WIDE lateral: the whole desk from the side, laptop open, the lone card small on the grain

blocks.vo_line: The counter climbs past eighteen hundred problems found. None of them is the reason your fan has run all afternoon.
blocks.through_line_state: six cards stacked, edges no longer flush
shots: CU eye-level: a cleaner application counter ticking upward through four digits on the laptop screen
WIDE high: the desk from above head height, the seated figure small, six grey cards piled at the corner
ECU lateral: the laptop vent seen edge-on, warm air visibly rippling the dust above it
MEDIUM low: a hand hovering over a bright coloured button without pressing it
CU overhead: the grey pile fanned apart, every stamped phrase vague and interchangeable

blocks.vo_line: Noah is a desktop app for macOS. It is not a chat window that hands you a Terminal command and wishes you luck.
blocks.through_line_state: twelve cards, the stack now upright and deliberate
shots: WIDE eye-level: a kitchen table in flat morning light, an open laptop beside a mug, the adult standing at the counter behind
CU high: the laptop screen showing a calm cream panel with generous margins and one short sentence
MEDIUM lateral: the adult sitting down and pulling the chair in, both hands settling either side of the machine
ECU low: a dense black terminal window on a second display, a long command line, cursor blinking
WIDE high: the kitchen table from above, twelve grey cards stacked against the table edge

blocks.vo_line: A browser tab cannot see your machine. Noah runs outside that sandbox, so it can read what your Mac is actually doing.
blocks.through_line_state: twenty cards, the stack as tall as the mug
shots: CU eye-level: a browser window filling the display, its edges pressed hard against a flat grey boundary
MEDIUM low: the adult pushing the browser aside, a rounded app tile visible on the dock below
ECU overhead: the app tile on the dock, a level horizon line drawn inside its rounded square
WIDE lateral: the kitchen seen from the side, the laptop small, everything daylit and unhurried
CU high: a plain list of running processes as neat rows, one single row marked warm amber

blocks.vo_line: You describe the symptom in your own words. My fan will not stop is a complete and valid bug report here.
blocks.through_line_state: the stack leaning against the sofa armrest
shots: WIDE eye-level: a living room sofa in afternoon light, a laptop resting on a cushion, the adult settled comfortably
ECU lateral: fingers typing one short plain sentence into a wide empty text field
CU high: the typed words on screen, large and plain, no jargon anywhere around them
MEDIUM low: the adult shrugging slightly at the machine, an ordinary unbothered gesture
WIDE overhead: the sofa from above, the grey stack propped against the armrest

blocks.vo_line: Noah runs audited diagnostics against troubleshooting playbooks that ship inside the app. They name the cause rather than counting things that look untidy.
blocks.through_line_state: top cards sliding, the stack near its limit
shots: CU high: a short numbered checklist advancing on screen, each step resolving to a small teal mark
WIDE low: the living room from floor height, the laptop lit, the room otherwise entirely still
MEDIUM lateral: the adult watching the screen with chin resting on one hand, patient
ECU overhead: one teal confirmation mark settling beside a named check
CU low: the grey stack leaning further, its uppermost cards beginning to slide

blocks.vo_line: The answer is usually dull and specific. A login item from an app you deleted, or stale preferences left behind by an update.
shots: WIDE eye-level: a narrow study nook beside a window, a laptop on a shelf desk, soft grey daylight
ECU high: one line of a file path rendered in plain monospace across the screen
MEDIUM low: the adult leaning in to read, glasses pushed up, eyebrows lifting slightly
CU lateral: a single row in a list marked warm amber while every other row stays plain
WIDE overhead: the nook from above, the grey stack now standing taller than the laptop lid

blocks.vo_line: Then Noah answers in plain English. One short sentence names the actual cause, and the next names exactly what it proposes to change.
blocks.through_line_state: the top card tilting off the stack
shots: CU high: two plain sentences appearing on a wide cream panel with nothing else on it
MEDIUM lateral: the adult reading, lips still, giving one unhurried nod
ECU low: the words stale preferences set in plain type, sharp and specific
WIDE eye-level: the study nook framed wide, window light flat, the machine quiet
CU overhead: the grey stack beside the keyboard, its top card tilting away

blocks.vo_line: Nothing runs until you approve. Every action appears on screen before it happens, and the button is yours to press or refuse.
shots: ECU eye-level: a single approve button carrying a blue to violet gradient bar, waiting and unpressed
MEDIUM low: a hand resting flat on the desk, deliberately not moving toward the trackpad
CU lateral: the exact proposed change written out above the button in one plain line
WIDE high: the sunlit desk from doorway height, the machine holding, nothing happening at all
CU overhead: a fingertip arriving on the trackpad and pressing once

blocks.vo_line: Every action is logged, and all of it is reversible. Noah moves the old file aside rather than deleting anything blind.
blocks.through_line_state: still tall, a single card lifted clear
shots: CU high: a plain log entry appearing with a small teal mark and a timestamp beside it
WIDE lateral: the desk from the side, the light warmer now, the grey stack beginning to slump
ECU low: a file name gaining a small backup suffix, the original sitting intact behind it
MEDIUM eye-level: the adult exhaling, shoulders dropping, hands leaving the keyboard
CU overhead: an undo control sitting plain and available beside the log

blocks.vo_line: Do not trust any of that. The desktop client is open source, so anyone can read what Noah is allowed to touch.
shots: ECU eye-level: plain readable source code scrolling slowly, calm and entirely unglamorous
MEDIUM high: the adult back at the kitchen table, scrolling the code with mild curiosity
WIDE low: the kitchen from chair height, daylight flat, three grey cards left on the table
CU lateral: a short permissions list written in plain words, every line kept brief
MEDIUM overhead: hands and laptop seen from above, the code still moving, unhurried

blocks.vo_line: One thousand eight hundred issues was never the count. It was always one, and the fan you heard all afternoon has stopped.
blocks.through_line_state: collapsed flat, leaving exactly one card face up
shots: CU high: the grey stack collapsing flat and leaving one card face up on the wood
MEDIUM eye-level: the adult standing beside the desk, laptop quiet and cool, mug in hand
ECU overhead: the single remaining card, the actual cause named across it in plain type
MEDIUM lateral: the adult lifting the mug and walking unhurried out of frame
WIDE low: the emptied desk, laptop lid half closed, a level line of light across the wall
